newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MRC Allied controlling stake changes hands.
newsitem.headline: MRC Allied controlling stake changes hands.

text.p: Real estate development firm MRC Allied Industries Inc said on Tuesday businessmen Benjamin Bitanga and Augusto Syjuco had taken a controlling stake in the company following a share sale by EMRO Holdings Inc.
EMRO, owned by presidential adviser for economic affairs Emilio Osmena, had sold 80 million shares representing 16 percent of MRC to Bitanga and his partner Syjuco, it said.
Under the deal, Benjamin Bitanga and Augusto Syjuco emerge with 45 percent of MRC Allied. EMRO's shareholding is reduced to 21.6 percent from a previous 37.6 percent.
The price of the shares was not disclosed.
"The purchase represents 16 percent of the company's outstanding shares of stock previously held by EMRO Holdings.
Bitanga's group previously had a 28.8 percent interest.
MRC sold 33.6 percent of its shares to the public in 1995.
Bitanga has interests in real estate development, while Syjuco, a prominent businessman in the southern Philippines, is involved in financial services.
Syjuco said he decided to invest in MRC after studying the potential of its industrial estate projects in the central Cebu and Leyte provinces.

"It is a major shift for us to go into real estate development, but considering that we are now building up our financial and banking businesses in the south and MRC is concentrating in the south as well, we thought the synergies are there, and one reinforces the other," he said.
MRC Allied closed five centavos lower at 3.35 pesos on Tuesday. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
